_comment: STE100 mode rules for ~/.claude/hooks/writing-preset-lint. Deterministic (not statistical, unlike the general lint-rules.json): every check here is a binary pass/fail per ASD-STE100 Issue 9 (2025-01-15). The not-approved/approved word lookup itself lives in ste100-dictionary.json, read separately by the hook. hard_bans use the same regex-with-optional-inline-flags format as lint-rules.json.

sentence_limits._comment: Rule 5.1 (procedural), Rule 6.3 (descriptive), Rule 5.5 (notes). A sentence is classified procedural if it's inside a numbered/lettered work-step list or starts with an imperative verb; otherwise descriptive. When classification is ambiguous the linter uses the looser (descriptive) cap to avoid false positives.

word_count_exceptions._comment: Rule 8.4-8.7 word-counting algorithm. Each pattern's matches are collapsed to a single counted token BEFORE splitting the sentence into words, applied in this order so longer/more-specific spans (parentheses, quotes) are protected before the narrower numeric/hyphen patterns run inside what's left outside them.

criteria: Passive voice used in procedural (instructional) text, or used in descriptive text where the agent is actually known or stated elsewhere - STE100 requires active voice except when the agent is genuinely unknown

An auxiliary-verb construction that isn't infinitive/imperative/simple present/simple past/simple future/past-participle-as-adjective (e.g. 'has installed', 'is being tested', 'can be adjusted', 'is to be removed') left un-rewritten
The '-ing' form used as a present-tense verb, a stand-alone adjective, or the head of a noun phrase with its own object, instead of only as a technical noun or a modifier inside a technical noun

A WARNING or CAUTION with the wrong risk level (injury/death mislabeled CAUTION, or a pure equipment-damage risk labeled WARNING), missing a leading command/condition, or missing a stated risk/consequence
More than one instruction packed into a single procedural sentence when the actions are not simultaneous and no result immediately follows its action
The same real-world item or concept referred to by two or more different technical nouns across the text (synonym rotation), instead of one consistent term
A multi-word noun longer than three words that was not shortened, hyphenated, or explained on first use
An invented phrasal verb (two approved words combined into a new, unapproved compound meaning) instead of the single approved verb that already covers it
A contraction, an omitted article, or an omitted 'that' after verbs like 'make sure'/'recommend' where its absence creates ambiguity
A gendered pronoun ('he'/'she') or a Latin abbreviation ('e.g.', 'i.e.', 'etc.') left unreplaced
